ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (No. 11 of 1987), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Acts 2008 and 2011, ss. 10–15, 53 and 55; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2017, ss. 7–14 and 30; Samoa International Financial Authority Act 2005; Financial Institutions Act 2015; Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Regulations 2018; SIFA AML/CFT Guidelines for Registered Agents and International Companies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarized passport copies and proof of residential address for each director, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of residence or nationality, with the passport issuing authority as original certifying source
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the issuing state; if the issuing state is not party to the HCCH 1961 Apostille Convention, consular legalization at a Samoa diplomatic mission or competent embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth declaration for each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or credit institution maintaining the account, plus notarization in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization through the competent foreign authority; bank letter must be dated within 90 days of submission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, and register of members for any corporate shareholder or corporate UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or Registrar of Companies in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by that jurisdiction's competent authority; otherwise consular legalization at the relevant embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of trust deed, declaration of trust, and register of beneficiaries for any trust acting as shareholder or UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Trustee, court, or notary public under the trust's governing law jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; court-issued extracts require certification by the issuing court registry

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized signatories and registered agents are subject to mandatory initial and ongoing screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, US Sectoral Sanctions Identifications, UK and EU consolidated sanctions lists, Samoa domestic sanctions and SIFA supervisory notices, and INTERPOL notices. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP, family member, or close associate of a PEP, and for any nominee shareholder arrangement. Screening is refreshed quarterly and before every material distribution or payment instruction; no exemption exists for offshore or international companies.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) International Company Registry Portal – Name Search and Reservation Module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All registered legal names must be in English or Samoan using Latin script, numerals and permitted punctuation only. Non-Latin scripts, including Chinese characters, are not accepted as the primary statutory name; any alternative non-Latin name must be preceded by or recorded as an approved transliteration of the Latin-script preferred name. The transliteration must be included in the constitutional documents and any Chinese-language founding documents require a certified English or Samoan translation for SIFA filing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations may be extended once for an additional 30 days upon written request and payment of the SIFA extension fee before the original validity window expires. If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a written administrative objection to the Registrar of International Companies at SIFA within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, setting out the grounds of appeal and attaching a revised name or a signed undertaking letter. The Registrar must decide the appeal within 10 business days. If the rejection is upheld or the Registrar remains silent, the applicant may apply by originating motion to the Supreme Court of Samoa for judicial review within 21 days of the decision date.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as a registered office. An International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at the premises of its licensed registered agent or other approved SIFA-licensed office, and that address must be available for service of process. Purely virtual office, mail-forwarding, or shared mailbox-only arrangements do not satisfy the statutory registered office requirement; remote administrative or advisory work may be performed from other locations but does not alter the registered office mandate.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of an unannounced physical on-site inspection is low to moderate for a standard low-risk consulting International Company, estimated at 15% probability in any given year and approximately 30% over a three-year supervisory cycle. The probability increases to 45% or higher if the UBO profile triggers PEP status, a sanctions hit, or adverse AML/CFT intelligence. SIFA and the Financial Intelligence Unit may conduct unannounced inspections of the registered agent's premises and demand production of UBO records, minute books, and client due diligence files within 48 hours.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2021; incorporating sections 7 (Incorporation), 9 (Memorandum and Articles), 10 (Statement of Compliance), and 11 (Registered Office)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Form 1) together with Statement of Compliance and Application for Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; share capital may be denominated in any currency and may remain unpaid at incorporation; no escrow account or capital deposit requirement for International Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers to the Memorandum of Association of the International Company hereby adopt the registered office at [Address], Apia, Samoa as the company's principal office; that the directors accept the allotment of one ordinary share of US$1.00 subscribed for each founding member; that the persons named as initial directors are appointed to the board pending the first general meeting; that the corporate seal be adopted; and that the directors be authorized to open bank accounts, execute any incorporation documents incidental to registration, and file the Statement of Compliance under the International Companies Act 1987. This resolution is effective forthwith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the MCIL Companies Online Portal or by physical lodgement at the Registry. Provide the proposed name with 'International Company' or 'Limited' suffix, clean name search certificate, and evidence of Professional Service Provider licence. Pay the name reservation fee and await approval before filing any constitutional documents.
required_dossiers: Passport copy and address proof of the licensed agent
Professional service provider licence of the incorporating agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or reserved conditionally, file an alternative name within 5 business days or submit a written appeal to the Registrar for reconsideration under section 7(4) of the International Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Charter Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MCIL in conjunction with a licensed International Company service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a licensed agent to prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association incorporating full permitted objects for tax structuring and advisory services, share allotment provisions, and directorship clauses. Ensure the Statement of Compliance is signed by the agent and notarized and that each subscriber's signature is authenticated. Retain draft copies for the statutory records.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statement of Compliance executed by the licensed agent
Notarized consent to act as initial director from each proposed director
Certified passport copies of directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the documents, correct the defect and resubmit within 10 business days; if notarization is defective, obtain fresh notarization from a Samoa-recognized notary public.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation package via the MCIL Companies Online Portal or at the Counter, Attach the notarized Memorandum and Articles, Form 1, Statement of Compliance, registered office consent, and appointment of registered agent. Pay the official state filing fee of US$100. The Certificate of Incorporation will be issued once the Registrar verifies compliance with the International Companies Act.
required_dossiers: Registered agent consent and appointment letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is refused or suspended, correct any identified discrepancies and submit a fresh application within 15 business days; alternatively request an expedited review with supporting legal justification. The Certificate of Incorporation may be reissued without additional operational delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Adoption of Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors, with documentation maintained through the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, either by physical attendance at the registered office or by electronic means consistent with the Articles. Adopt the first board resolution covering the registered office address, director appointments, share issuance, and banking authorities. Ensure the minutes, share register, register of directors, and register of charges are opened and maintained at the registered office in Samoa.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the inaugural board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the resolution or minutes are found defective, cure by drafting and executing a corrective board resolution and lodging a certified copy with the registered agent within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Bank Account Activation and AML Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial banks in Samoa / Offshore Banking Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account by presenting the Certificate of Incorporation, certified Memorandum and Articles, first board resolution, and beneficial ownership declaration to a bank with offshore banking capability. Complete the bank's know-your-customer and anti-money laundering onboarding procedures, including source of funds and business activity confirmation. The bank may require an opinion letter from the licensed agent confirming the low-risk advisory nature of the entity.
required_dossiers: First board resolution on banking authorization
Passport copies and proof of address for directors and ultimate beneficial owners
Business activity description and source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank misfiles or requests supplementary information, provide a complete beneficial ownership chart, certified translation of any non-English documents, and an updated corporate profile letter from the registered agent. Re-submit within 5 business days of the bank's query.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Companies and International Trusts Unit
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificate of Compliance – Offshore Service Provider Business Licence (Category B: International Tax and Investment Advisory)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) – Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Category 3 – Low Impact Professional Services); no full EIA Report required for office-based consultancy operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or point-source VOC emissions expected; comply with the Water Resources Management Act 2008 for sanitary discharge, the Solid Waste Regulations for segregated disposal of paper and electronic waste, and the Noise Control Standards of Samoa for office decibel levels below 60 dB(A) during operating hours

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA) confirming compliant fire extinguishers and emergency egress; structural load inspection certificate from the MCIL Building Inspectorate for the registered office; occupational health and workplace clearance from the Ministry of Labour confirming compliance with the Samoa National Building Code and safe office occupancy limits

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Apia; official portal: www.sra.gov.ws, e-filing via the STARS online revenue system. International Companies are regulated by the Registrar of International Companies / Corporate and Business Registry (CBR), Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign owners incorporate a Samoa International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), solely through a licensed registered agent. Step 1: file Articles/Certificate of Incorporation (Chinese-language articles permitted) with the Registrar; Step 2: obtain Certificate of Incorporation and pay registration fee; Step 3: the IC is statutorily exempt from income tax and VAGST and therefore does not apply for a Samoan TIN/VAT ID; Step 4: file the annual return and pay the annual government fee to CBR by 30 June; Step 5: a TIN from SRA (Form IRD-1) is required only if the entity nevertheless undertakes a taxable activity, which is generally prohibited for ICs; Step 6: if the IC qualifies as an investment entity under CRS/AEOI, it must separately register with SRA as a Reporting Financial Institution.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (International Companies Act 1987 s.114: full exemption from Samoan income tax, stamp duty, capital gains tax and all other Samoan taxes for 20 years from incorporation, renewable for a further 5 years; wholly offshore territorial scope; exemption conditional on prohibition of trading with Samoan residents and on derivation of no Samoan-source income)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Samoan check-the-box, US Section 7701, or hybrid-mismatch election exists; the tax exemption is automatic by statute. Available elections: (i) elect the IC's financial year-end and accounting currency under the ICA; (ii) apply to the Minister for a 5-year extension of the 20-year exemption; (iii) elect express versus standard incorporation; (iv) elect redomiciliation into or out of Samoa. For US federal tax purposes, classification of the Samoa IC is determined by the beneficial owner's US check-the-box election, not by Samoan law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) under the VAGST Act 1997-1998 (as amended), administered by the Samoa Revenue Authority
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: SAT$150,000 annual value of taxable supplies made in Samoa (compulsory registration); voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold. International Companies carrying on wholly offshore activities are outside the scope of VAGST because they are prohibited from making taxable supplies to Samoan residents.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-mandated e-invoicing, or digital stamping regime exists in Samoa. Registered persons must issue standard VAGST tax invoices (paper or PDF), retain records for at least 5 years, and file periodic VAGST returns through SRA's STARS e-services portal; compliance is enforced through periodic audit rather than transactional electronic validation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods, and services supplied to and consumed wholly outside Samoa (including offshore professional and management consultancy services to non-residents), are zero-rated under the VAGST Act 1997-1998 s.9. The supplier must evidence physical export or offshore supply and retain the contract, logistics, and payment records. A Samoa IC engaged purely in cross-border tax structuring and advisory services to non-residents has no Samoan VAGST exposure and will not need to claim zero-rating or refunds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Samoa Customs Export Declaration (CusDec) endorsed by Samoa Customs for physical exports
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export from Samoa (not applicable to pure offshore consultancy services)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT credit advice evidencing settlement of the exported supply
Executed service agreement and zero-rated supplies declaration for cross-border professional services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Samoa imposes no foreign-exchange controls, and therefore no statutory export-proceeds repatriation deadline applies to ICs. However, the Samoa Revenue Authority may impose penalty tax of up to 150% of any VAGST shortfall, daily late-filing penalties, and interest under the VAGST Act 1997-1998 and the Tax Administration Act 2012. Fraudulent zero-rating and refund claims are clawed back in full with interest and penal assessments, and expose the offender to criminal fines and imprisonment under the Crimes Act 2013. An IC that breaches the International Companies Act restrictions on trading with Samoan residents forfeits its statutory tax exemption retroactively and becomes taxable on all Samoan-source income.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS / Fa'aputugatupe Tutotonu o Samoa), operating under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984 and exercising delegated exchange-control functions under the Exchange Control Act 1976 (as amended); it is the sole licensing, foreign-exchange, payment-system, and sanctions-screening authority for all banks and money transfer operators in Samoa.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is a current-account convertible currency under Samoa's IMF Article VIII obligations; current-account payments (trade, services, fees) are free from CBS restrictions, but the capital account remains regulated and requires prior CBS approval through a licensed commercial bank. A Samoan International Company (IC) is treated as a non-resident offshore entity: its foreign-currency accounts may be credited and disbursed offshore without CBS prior approval, and dividends, management fees, and liquidation proceeds remitted to non-resident shareholders are exempt from Samoan income tax, withholding tax, and FX conversion controls. Profit remittance hurdles arise only when funds are converted into WST or credited to a domestic onshore account, in which case the remitting bank must undertake CBS external-transaction reporting and, for amounts above the bank's delegated threshold, obtain CBS scheduled-payment approval; a tax clearance certificate from the Samoa Ministry of Revenue and an audited or management-prepared financial statement demonstrating settled liabilities are standard conditions for any onshore-account outward remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Samoan legislation requires all export and service-export proceeds (including cross-border consultancy fees) to be repatriated to Samoa within 30 calendar days from the date of receipt abroad and surrendered to a CBS-licensed dealer bank for conversion into WST, with a mandatory conversion ratio of 100% of the proceeds, unless the exporter holds a CBS-approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) exemption that permits retention of up to 100% of proceeds in foreign currency for verified operational needs. For a non-resident International Company, the 30-day surrender obligation is disapplied where the CBS/registered bank records the IC as a non-resident entity and the receipts are credited to a designated offshore or non-resident FCY account; however, if the IC's fees are routed through a domestic WST account, the full surrender rule reactivates and conversion into WST is mandatory.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Non-Resident Operational USD/AUD/WST Multi-Currency Account (Class B offshore account)
Capital Escrow USD Account plus Operational WST/USD Account for International Companies

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ) – Samoa Branch
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Non-Resident Operational USD/AUD/NZD Account with correspondent-bank clearing in Sydney
Resident Operational WST Account only; foreign-currency account requires CBS prior approval

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. Samoa has not enacted an electronic-money-institution (EMI) or payment-service-provider licensing regime, and no domestic fintech offers offshore USD treasury accounts; offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut, Mercury) generally decline to onboard Samoan International Companies because of correspondent-bank de-risking, the absence of a Samoan regulatory passport, and FATF-style jurisdictional due-diligence friction. The practical legal constraint is that an EMI domiciled in Australia, the UK, or the EU cannot maintain a WST settlement account with CBS, and a Samoan IC cannot obtain an independent EMI license; the recommended architecture is a primary account at BSP or SCB supplemented by a separately regulated Australian or New Zealand International Merchant Account for card-clearing and low-value disbursements, with all FX conversion executed through the licensed Samoan dealer bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Fully remote onboarding is technically permitted by BSP, ANZ, and SCB for non-resident International Companies provided that (i) all constitutional documents (Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, register of directors and shareholders) are apostilled and notarized, (ii) all directors and the beneficial owner pass a live video-conference KYC interview, (iii) a compliance reference letter is provided by a SIFA-licensed registered agent in Apia, and (iv) board resolutions authorizing account opening and signatories are notarized; National Bank of Samoa mandates in-person appearance of at least one director in Apia. In practice, a single physical visit to Apia by one director to sign the bank mandate and meet the AML/CFT officer materially reduces approval time from 4-6 weeks to 5-10 business days and is strongly recommended as a de-risking measure; CBS-supervised banks may also require an economic-substance declaration confirming that the IC's 7020 tax-consulting activity is performed for non-resident clients and does not create local taxable presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: offshore 'tax structuring consultancy' descriptor combined with no physical office or local substance in Samoa
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Incorporation; SIFA registered-agent consent letter; notarized board resolution; IC annual return filing receipt; economic-substance declaration (non-resident advisory activity); evidence of offshore client contracts and invoices; third-party corporate verification report (World-Check or Refinitiv) showing no adverse media.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound share-capital injection from a foreign trust, nominee shareholder, or family holding structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth statement for each contributing entity; 12 months of originating bank statements; certified trust deed and beneficial-ownership register; notarized declarations of trust/nominee arrangements; independent tax and legal opinion on the funding structure; KYB/UBO information aligned to FATF Recommendation 24.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment patterns to low-tax or high-risk jurisdictions inconsistent with the stated consultancy business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete service-agreement files; structured fee schedules and time/expense breakdowns; client-side sanctions and PEP screening results; geographic risk matrix and jurisdiction restriction policy; tax-residency certificates of counterparties; commitment to CDD refresh every 12 months and transaction-monitoring alerts to the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Credit-card acquiring for consultancy fees, triggering chargeback and cross-border selling scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI-DSS SAQ-A attestation; processor and gateway agreements; chargeback management and refund policy targeting a ratio below 0.9%; delivered-advisory-work evidence (engagement letters, material output records); customer complaint and dispute-resolution process; accurate merchant category code and descriptor registration with the acquiring bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of nominee directors or a corporate services provider as registered shareholder creating a concealed-ownership red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written nominee agreement and declaration; confidential Beneficial Ownership Register filed with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA); identification of the settlor and ultimate natural persons; signed indemnities from the corporate services provider; group-structure chart linking WS_IC to the ultimate parent; legal opinion confirming compliance with the International Companies Act 1987.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing is via SWIFT MT103 from the parent or shareholder's bank to the IC's non-resident USD account at BSP or SCB, using the Samoan Bank-Branch Identifier plus the IC's account number and the narrative purpose code 'Share Capital – Direct Investment Equity' together with the statement 'Subscription for shares under the International Companies Act 1987'; the remitting bank must classify the payment under IMF BPM6 Direct Investment – Equity (other than reinvestment of earnings), and the receiving Samoan bank records the credit in CBS External-Transaction Reporting (ETR) with a note that the beneficiary is a non-resident IC, thereby avoiding onshore surrender. Verification required by the receiving bank comprises a certified board resolution approving the share allotment, an extract from the share register showing the subscriber, the Certificate of Incorporation, proof of payment of the SIFA annual fee, and a registered-agent compliance letter; credits to a domestic WST account would additionally require CBS approval, an FX dealing slip, and a copy of the applicable Samoan tax registration, so the non-resident FCY routing is strongly preferred.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational trade disbursements (subcontractor fees, software licenses, professional indemnity premiums, and client-reimbursable expenses) are cleared via SWIFT MT103 with charges option 'OUR' to guarantee full value to beneficiaries; larger structured procurements may use an advised Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) issued by BSP or ANZ with documents handled through the Australian/NZ correspondent corridor, and any domestic WST payments for local registered-agent or government fees settle through the CBS-operated Real-Time Gross Settlement system in Apia. Credit-card inflows are captured through the Visa/Mastercard acquiring service of BSP Samoa or SCB, with daily settlement into the IC's WST operational account and an automatic USD/WST conversion executed at the bank's daily dealing rate; the IC should maintain a segregated USD clearing account to minimize conversion friction and should require card acquirers to remit settlement in USD where the scheme permits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore outright USD/WST forward contracts with BSP, ANZ, or SCB for tenors up to 12 months, requiring an underlying current-account or capital-account exposure and CBS reporting; the instruments settle by net delivery in WST at maturity.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST quoted by Sydney, Singapore, and Hong Kong counterparties for non-resident ICs, with USD cash settlement on a notional principal and reference rate based on the CBS published mid-rate; no domestic CBS approval applies because settlement occurs entirely outside Samoa.

Cross-currency swaps (USD/AUD/NZD versus WST) executed offshore between the IC and an international bank, limited to risk-management of forecast fee revenue and exempt from CBS approval for non-resident accounts; onshore-referenced swaps require prior CBS capital-account authorization.

European-style FX options on WST purchased from international prime brokers or the Samoan dealing banks for hedging invoice exposure, with premiums payable in USD from the non-resident account; writing of options by the IC is not permissible without CBS authorization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of International Company (Form for confirmation of registered office, directors, members and compliance status)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Independent State of Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of incorporation; preservation of the date is mandatory and the return is filed with the annual renewal fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty accrues at 5% per month or part thereof; continued non-filing for more than 6 months may trigger administrative strike-off of the company from the International Companies Register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual License Renewal Fee (Government Annual Fee for International Company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – International Companies Registry, Government of Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by the anniversary of incorporation; invoiced by the registered agent approximately 30 days before the due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A fixed late penalty of US$100 plus 5% per month interest; strike-off proceedings may be commenced after a 3-month delinquency period

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Economic Substance Declaration (Substance Return for Non-Resident Service Providers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Registrar of International Companies (Economic Substance Compliance Unit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months of the entity's accounting reference date; for an International Company electing a non-December financial year, within the stated filing period aligned to the accounting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Filing of a false statement is a criminal offence; failure to file may attract Penalties under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Act and may be notified to the Financial Intelligence Unit

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a Samoa International Company engaged in tax structuring and transfer pricing advisory activities, provided it is not a public company, licensed financial institution, or insurance undertaking. An audit becomes mandatory only if shareholders holding at least 25% of the voting rights request one or if the company is subject to a consolidated group audit under its parent jurisdiction.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No specific accounting framework mandated for exempt International Companies; if financial statements are prepared, International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (US GAAP) are commonly adopted for commercial and lending purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: In addition to the annual return, the registered agent must keep and update the register of beneficial owners. No separate shareholding-transfer declaration is required annually, but every transfer of shares during the year must be recorded in the Register of Members, and the beneficial owner register must be made available to the Registrar upon request. A formal annual UBO confirmation is furnished by the registered agent to the Registrar as part of the statutory records review.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes of Shareholders and Directors Meetings (Minute Book)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$500 – US$1,500 per annum depending on capital, number of directors and corporate service bundle
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$0 (exempt) or US$1,500 – US$4,500 if a voluntary opinion is obtained for cross-border financing or investor due diligence

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (resident taxable company rate, applied to taxable income exceeding WST 10,000, with a 15% rate on the first WST 10,000); 0% for a registered International Company under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Company (Tax-Exempt Zone): full exemption from income tax, capital gains tax, estate duty, stamp duty, and exchange control; no withholding tax on distributions to non-residents; fixed annual government fee substitutes for income tax; offshore consulting and tax-structuring fees are outside the Samoa tax net unless derived from Samoa-source activity

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Company Income Tax Return (SRC Form CIR-1) lodged through the Samoa Revenue Corporation (SRC) electronic filing portal (TAP - Taxpayer Access Point)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (quarterly provisional tax instalments required where prior-year net tax exceeds WST 10,000)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end (30 June for a calendar-year taxpayer); provisional instalment deadlines: 31 May, 31 August, 30 November, and 28 February

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income (Samoa-source and foreign active income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Samoa-source income; offshore tax-structuring consultancy fees earned by the International Company are excluded and scheduled as exempt income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income, including International Company exempt income under section 6 of the International Companies Act
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the exemption schedule and a declaration by the licensed registered agent confirming continued IC status to preserve the 0% effective rate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions (staff costs, rent, professional fees, depreciation, interest)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses directly attributable to taxable Samoa-source income; intra-group charges must satisfy arm's length rules and contemporaneous documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying the 5-year loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An International Company with no Samoa-source income enters nil; losses of a taxable branch may be carried forward for only 5 years and cannot be offset against exempt offshore income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable at 27% (15% on the first WST 10,000 for qualifying small resident companies)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0 for a fully exempt International Company; resident-branch taxpayers must compute tax on Samoa-source income only

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax paid and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form IR-21 for foreign tax credit claims; credits are limited to Samoa tax attributable to the same income category

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Authorize the Samoa licensed registered agent to execute and pay; non-resident principals must retain SRC taxpayer registration and a local service address

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: WST 500 per month, capped at WST 5,000; late payment: 5% of unpaid tax plus 2% monthly compounding interest; default assessments under the Tax Administration Act 2012; criminal fines up to WST 100,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for fraudulent returns

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return and Government Fee Confirmation for International Companies (registered with the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, in conjunction with SRC records)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (on the registration anniversary; government fee cycle aligned to the calendar year)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within one month after the annual incorporation anniversary; annual government fee payable before 1 November in each year (WST 3,000 to WST 5,000 depending on share capital tier)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, International Company number, and date of incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners must ensure the registered name does not imply prohibited banking, insurance, or trust business without a license

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office in Samoa and licensed registered agent details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Samoa-licensed International Company Service Provider must countersign; this address is the legal seat for service of process and tax notices

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors, shareholders, and beneficial ownership register
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the ultimate beneficial owner schedule; maintain the register at the registered agent's office for AML inspection; nominee arrangements must be disclosed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of continued tax-exempt status and absence of Samoa-source business
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Certify that no consulting revenue is derived from Samoa residents or Samoa property; false certification exposes the IC to revocation of exempt status

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Annual fee arrears: WST 50 per month late surcharge; failure to file leads to registrar strike-off, forfeiture of assets to the State, and loss of the ability to enforce contracts in Samoa courts; directors trading after strike-off incur personal liability

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on gross dividends paid by a resident taxable Samoa company to a non-resident shareholder; 0% for a registered International Company distributing profit to non-resident shareholders under the International Companies Act statutory exemption
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: File SRC Form WHT-R (Application for Withholding Tax Relief) before payment; attach the recipient's Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), a treaty entitlement declaration, and supporting beneficiary ownership statements; obtain SRC endorsement before the reduced rate is applied; Samoa's limited DTA network (Australia, New Zealand) requires the recipient to be the beneficial owner and to satisfy any limitation-of-benefits clause
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 10% on payments to non-residents (0% under the IC exemption if derived from exempt IC assets); royalties: statutory 15% (0% under the IC exemption); treaty-reduced rates generally 10% for interest and 5% to 10% for royalties, subject to TRC submission and SRC relief endorsement

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory where annual cross-border related-party transactions exceed WST 1,000,000 or intra-group service charges exceed WST 500,000; Master File: mandatory where the consolidated group revenue exceeds WST 10,000,000; an International Company in the exempt zone is generally outside SRC's transfer pricing compliance net unless it operates a resident taxable branch or earns Samoa-source income
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No standalone Samoa Economic Substance Regulations statute for International Companies; substance is evaluated through the registered office in Samoa, the engagement of a licensed registered agent, real board meetings and minutes, staffing and professional competence in the tax-structuring consultancy, and independent funding; the OECD/EU substance framework and Samoa's place-of-effective-management test under the Income Tax Act 2012 govern treaty access and foreign CFC reclassification; letterbox entities are vulnerable to foreign anti-abuse rules, EU list sanctions, and Samoan registrar strike-off

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Structuring
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing taxable Samoa-source consultancy fees through the exempt International Company, issuing false invoices for fictitious offshore advisory services, or backdating service contracts to shift profits from an active Samoa-resident business into the tax-exempt IC shell
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Administration Act 2012 sections 85-87: penalty of up to 150% of the tax evaded, additional civil penalties up to WST 100,000, criminal conviction with imprisonment up to 5 years, and deregistration of the International Company by the Registrar
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax and penalties; foreign directors face travel bans, international arrest notifications, and civil restitution orders; fraudulent misuse of the corporate form pierces the corporate veil and exposes personal assets

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse / Deficient Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the International Company as a letterbox arrangement with no Samoa registered agent oversight, no accounting records, no board meetings in Samoa, and unrelated backdated contracts used to strip profits from operating jurisdictions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Registrar powers under the International Companies Act: strike-off, restoration conditions, and financial penalties up to WST 250,000; foreign-tax reclassification removes the IC exemption and triggers back-tax assessments with penalties in the operating jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly certify false substance declarations commit a criminal offence; the corporate veil is pierced for fraud; directors are personally liable for refunds and tax restatements arising from the collapsed structure

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain a beneficial ownership register, using undisclosed nominee shareholders, or accepting high-risk client payments without customer due diligence in the cross-border tax-structuring consultancy
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Samoa Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018: civil penalties up to WST 500,000, custodial sentences up to 14 years, asset forfeiture, and mandatory reporting obligations to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit; licensed agent revocation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally criminally liable; travel bans and INTERPOL red notices are available; professional disqualification of the directors from acting as International Company service providers

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fiscal Non-Compliance (Annual Filings and Withholding Duties)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repeated non-payment of annual government fees, failure to declare and remit Samoa withholding tax on any resident-source payments, and continued trading after the Registrar's strike-off notice
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late fee surcharges of 50% of unpaid fees, automatic strike-off, disqualification from suing in Samoa courts, and revenue debts attaching to the IC's Samoa bank accounts; SRC may impose daily default assessments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who act after strike-off are personally liable for all debts incurred; unpaid withholding tax imposes a director's personal statutory duty; travel bans are issued for unresolved revenue assessments exceeding WST 50,000
